title: Reject authored code that loses its real source or typecheck

AC-1.proof: The gate inventories 8 blocks over 7 documents; the test's independently written scanner derives the same identity set; every block resolves to exactly 1 committed source file or a sha256+length-pinned region (region bindings proven to match exactly 1 window in their source); both engine owner compilers and the live-example import-graph compiler ran with exit 0 in real dependency contexts (receipts name executable, cwd, config, args, duration, TypeScript 6.0.3).

AC-2.proof: On fresh owned corpus copies: removed quickstart-messages.ts -> exit nonzero naming document quickstart.mdx, snippet messagesSource, source path, 'missing source'; the theming.mdx css region removed from apps/example/global.css -> exit nonzero naming theming.mdx, fence-0, global.css, region; the region duplicated -> exit nonzero 'ambiguous selection'; all bindings removed while code retained -> exit nonzero naming all six document/snippet identities with 'no committed binding'; restored bindings -> exit 0 with the original inventory; missing discovery root and empty discovery root -> exit nonzero with explicit discovery diagnostics.

AC-3.proof: A real astro build over an owned repo-shaped scratch copy (with a proof page rendering SourceSnippet for a whole-file selection and a named multiline region of quickstart-screen.tsx retaining interior indentation and its final newline) served on an owned ephemeral port and driven by real Chromium: rendered code textContent and navigator.clipboard.readText() after clicking each snippet's real Copy control equal the selected source byte-for-byte (length + sha256 equality asserted). The production --check-emitted comparison passed the untouched dist (2 elements, 0 failures) and rejected a one-byte drift in a fresh physical dist copy with document/snippet/source identity and mismatch offset, leaving the corrupted artifact byte-identical (no silent re-emission).

AC-4.proof: Unchanged receipts: 3 compiler receipts exit 0 with executable/config/args/TypeScript-version identities. Per engine (fresh corpus copies): import mutated to '@/shared/__ori_ast_005_missing__' -> nonzero through the real tsc with the marker and document/snippet/source identities; '<QuickstartScreen __ori_ast_005_invalid_prop__ />' -> nonzero through real tsc with the marker. Missing prerequisites: engine tsconfig.json removed -> nonzero naming the owning compiler context; whole uniwind package removed -> nonzero naming packages/docs-snippets/uniwind; node_modules/react-native removed from the real assembled consumer -> real compiler diagnostics name react-native (the dependency), then pnpm install restores it and the unchanged corpus passes again with exit 0.

interpretation_notes: AC-1's 'coverage includes 5 code kinds: TS, TSX, shell, CSS and configuration' is observed as: TS, TSX, shell and CSS coverage comes from the 8 real authored blocks (2 displayed identities each for the shared TS and TSX sources); configuration coverage comes from the two engine packages' 16 committed configuration files, which the gate requires present and records under kindCoverage.configuration and configurationInputs. The authored corpus contains no configuration-language fenced block or readFileSync-bound configuration file — apps/docs/src/content/** is write-prohibited to this task — so a configuration-kind authored block could not be created without violating scope. The gate's kind taxonomy and provenance machinery cover configuration fences the moment the corpus gains one.

The discovery root is ORI-AST-001's authored substrate (apps/docs/src/content/docs/**). apps/example/docs/live-chat.md, apps/example/README.md and apps/harness/README.md contain handwritten bash fences with no committed source; the task contract rejects handwritten unbound fences, so including them would make the unchanged corpus fail AC-1 by construction.

Engine owner compilers run against the committed consumer recipe executed verbatim (pnpm install, expo reconcile, the five public registry installs, the recipe's own tsc step) inside an owned cache keyed by dependency identity; every compile case then clones the assembled consumer, syncs the CURRENT corpus sources in, and runs the consumer's own tsc --noEmit. The cache lives under --consumer-cache (default <tmpdir>/ori-ast-005-consumers) and is the gate's only persistent write surface.
Region bindings pin the selection by sha256 + BYTE length; JS-string lengths differ from byte lengths on the seed text (multibyte em dashes), which the tests account for with Buffer.byteLength.
cleanup: All mutation corpus copies, compile case dirs, and the scratch docs app are removed on every exit path (mkdtemp + rmSync in finally/afterAll).
Owned probe consumers and clone probes from environment validation were deleted from the OS temp dir.

The persistent consumer cache (<tmpdir>/ori-ast-005-consumers and the manual /tmp/ori-ast-005-green-cache) remains by design as the gate's documented cache; no listener from this task remains (previews were spawned on ephemeral owned ports and killed in finally).
